Great news — your friend is right! SWISS does offer a **"Pay per invoice"** option. Here's everything you need to know, per the **Pay per invoice** section of the SWISS FAQ:

---

### ✅ Who qualifies?
You must meet **all three** of the following criteria:
- **Over 18 years old**
- **Resident of Switzerland or the Principality of Liechtenstein**
- **Flying from Switzerland** (this payment option is only available for flights departing from Switzerland)

---

### 🔍 How does it work?
1. **ID verification:** You'll need to complete a one-time ID scan (photo of your document + a selfie) via a link sent to your smartphone. Once passed, you won't need to repeat it for future bookings.
2. **Credit check:** SWISS's partner **POWERPAY** performs an online check. It may be declined due to creditworthiness, contradictory information, or unpaid POWERPAY invoices.
3. **You can board your flight** regardless of whether you've paid the invoice yet.

---

### 📄 When and how do you pay?
- You'll receive an **individual invoice by email within 24–48 hours**, issued free of charge.
- **Payment deadline:** 15 days from receipt of the email (via online banking; post office payments incur third-party costs).
- If you don't pay the individual invoice on time, outstanding amounts are rolled into a **monthly invoice**, sent by post around the middle of the following month — this incurs a **CHF 2.90 fee**.

---

### ❌ What if I cancel?
- If already paid: you'll receive a refund by bank transfer.
- If not yet paid and SWISS notifies POWERPAY in time: a revised invoice is issued.

---

If you meet the eligibility criteria, you can select "Pay per invoice" as your payment method at checkout. If you have any issues with the process, I'd recommend contacting SWISS directly for further assistance.

Great news — the policy is clear on this. Here's what you need to know, per the **Ordering an invoice** section:

---

### Your e-ticket confirmation is sufficient in most cases

> *"Your e-ticket confirmation is internationally recognised as a receipt in most countries, including Switzerland, and it can be used for the reimbursement of expenses and for the submission of a tax return."*

So in the majority of cases — including Switzerland — **you do not need a special invoice**. Your existing e-ticket confirmation (booking confirmation) is the accepted document.

---

### How to access it

You can retrieve your e-ticket confirmation in your SWISS profile under **"Bookings"**, via either:
- the **"E-documents (Invoice)"** link, or
- the **"Passenger Receipt"** link.

---

### If your country has special requirements

> *"For countries with special requirements, an invoice can be ordered using forms that are available for this purpose."*

In that case, a separate invoice can be ordered.

---

### Timing & fees (per the **Invoice Questions** section)

- **Free of charge** if requested within **90 days** after the ticket has been fully used.
- After that, a fee of **CHF 30 per transaction** applies (up to a maximum of five e-ticket confirmations).

---

**In short:** For most tax filings, your e-ticket confirmation is all you need. Just download it from your profile. If your local tax authority requires a different format, contact SWISS to order a formal invoice.

You can avoid this by using SWISS's currency conversion option and paying in your card's own currency — the exchange rate is then locked in at the time of booking.

2. **Other bank charges:** Some banks might charge additional fees in individual cases. SWISS has no influence over these charges.

So in short: **no extra cost from SWISS for using a credit card**, but check with your bank about any foreign currency or transaction fees on their end.

Hope that helps — feel free to complete your checkout with confidence! ✈️
